    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">The link between agriculture and innovation has been a central part of Hamilton's economic landscape for decades and is celebrated annually at <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/fieldaysnz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Fieldays®</a>.

The event brings together Waikato businesses like <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/gallagher?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Gallagher</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/lic_2?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Livestock Improvement Corporation (LIC)</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/agrisea-nz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>AgriSea</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/waikato-milking-systems?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Waikato Milking Systems</a>, along with hundreds of others from across the primary sector.

Attendance was up by 20% compared to last year, but as <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nznfs?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>New Zealand National Fieldays Society</a> CE <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/richard-lindroos-50019256?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Richard Lindroos</a> said, “beyond the numbers, success isn’t just reflected in attendance figures, it’s seen in the energy on site, the conversations happening, and the genuine connections being made.” 

That culture of collaboration permeates our region as a long-standing core value and a differentiator in attracting business investment and talent.
 
Download "A New Perspective" (link in comments) to discover what makes Hamilton an ideal base for meaningful work that can have a global impact.</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">It’s been another strong result for our Communication and Engagement team at last week’s national <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/prinz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>PRINZ - Public Relations Institute of New Zealand</a> Awards.

Our Election 2025 – breaking down barriers campaign, which encouraged Hamiltonians to take part in the local elections and vote in the Maaori Ward poll, picked up both Gold and Bronze. The work focused on helping people understand why voting matters and supporting more people to have their say.

The awards recognise clear strategy, strong delivery, and measurable impact. This was a complex campaign with tight timeframes and a wide audience, and it drove strong engagement across the city, with the election turnout rising to 33% (from 29.4% in 2022) - a 12.24% proportional increase. 

This success also reflects a strong partnership approach, with a special ngaa mihi to Waikato-Tainui and our other community partners for their collaboration and support throughout the campaign.

This marks a second consecutive year the team has taken out Gold in the Community Relations and Engagement category, following last year’s success with the Hamilton Gardens Paid Entry campaign.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We're taking a proactive step toward the biggest shake-up of local government in decades by choosing to go for the Government’s ‘Head Start’ reform pathway. 

So, what does that mean?
We’ll be developing a proposal by 9 August 2026 that outlines how local government could be improved for our communities – creating a new system that is more fit for purpose. This may involve a merger with one or more councils to become a unitary authority, that would also deliver regional council responsibilities.

This is a significant moment and an opportunity to shape our future, rather than risk decisions being made for us later.
We know there’s a lot to consider, and the timeframes are tight.
